name: Urban Transitions Lab. Co-Designing Sustainable Change
description:
Urban Infrastructure+: Design Sprint
"Leveraging Infrastructure Renewal for Liveable Urban Spaces" 

In the winter semester 2026/27, the Design Sprint focuses on large-scale transformation processes of urban infrastructure, using the Donnersbergerbrücke in Munich as a case study. The replacement of this transport infrastructure, scheduled for completion by 2040, is intended not only to create a functioning multimodal transport corridor and mobility hub, but also to use the transformation process as an opportunity to create a greener and more attractive environment providing high-quality urban spaces for the local community.

Achieving these objectives involves complex spatial, infrastructural, institutional and procedural framework conditions and path dependencies. During the Design Sprint, students explore these interdependencies and develop context-sensitive and sustainable transformation strategies.

Based on different transformation scenarios, students work in interdisciplinary groups to develop, design and visualise plausible spatial project proposals. Particular emphasis is placed on communicating complex framework conditions and interdependencies in a way that makes them accessible and open to discussion for a broader, non-expert audience.

The results will be presented and discussed with representatives from academia and urban governance.

The Design Sprint builds on the thematic framework of the “Urban Infrastructure+: Preparatory Seminar” (LV 0000002945). A selection of the transformation scenarios developed during the seminar will serve as a starting point for the project work during the Design Sprint. Prior participation in the Preparatory Seminar is not required; the necessary background material will be provided as part of the Design Sprint.
prerequisites:
Prospective students should have a strong disciplinary background and experience in project work in their respective fields, demonstrate an interest in urban transformation, and be motivated to apply their knowledge to real-world problems while collaborating in interdisciplinary groups.

The ability to work with visual tools and representation methods (analogue/digital) is not a formal requirement but is recommended. Students should also be able to present complex content effectively.

Prior participation in the Preparatory Seminar is not a prerequisite for participation in the Design Sprint.
